findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - concurrent runs exhaust the shared GraphQL quota.
GitHub can return `API rate limit already exceeded` in a GraphQL error, as shown in [GitHub CLI's issue tracker](https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/12812). The new matcher requires `API rate limit exceeded` without `already`, so it returns the error before reaching the repaired GraphQL quota lookup. For example, merge's `gh pr view` at `src/forge/merge.py:66` then refuses instead of waiting. Close's history rebuild and land's queue also make GraphQL calls. This repair regresses the main rate-limit recovery path.
findings.title: Not done: When GitHub answers with a rate-limit error, close, merge and land wait until the reset time GitHub reports

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - concurrent close or merge requests hit a secondary GitHub rate limit with a Retry-After header.
The parser searches only `gh`'s output, but [gh api prints response headers only when requested](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/v2.83.2/pkg/cmd/api/api.go#L420-L425). The close and merge check request at `src/forge/checks.py:622` does not request them. If GitHub reports `Retry-After: 180`, this code instead announces a 60-second wait and retries early, repeatedly ignoring GitHub's reported time. The repair's test supplies the header directly in the stub's stderr, so it does not demonstrate that the real command exposes it.
findings.title: Functional: Honor the retry time for secondary limits

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - GitHub exhausts the GraphQL quota or its response header differs from the quota endpoint.
The repaired GraphQL case still supplies `API rate limit exceeded`, while a real GitHub response can say `API rate limit already exceeded`; production returns that response without waiting, yet this proof passes. The header case also injects a response header into a `gh pr edit` error, although [gh's error formatter](https://github.com/cli/go-gh/blob/v2.13.0/pkg/api/errors.go#L28-L35) does not print those headers. The named proof therefore still passes while GraphQL recovery and real response-header precedence are broken.
